results.title: Canada at World Cup 2026: form & Sofascore Rating
highlights:
Canada step into the FIFA World Cup 2026 with something they have never carried to this stage before: momentum and a realistic path out of the group. Hosting duties help, but the schedule matters too. Group B pairs the Canada national team with Bosnia and Herzegovina, Qatar and Switzerland, a mix that looks more manageable than their last two World Cups. History is still a motivator. Canada waited 36 years to score their first World Cup goal, finally doing it in 2022. The next box to tick is their first World Cup win. With Sofascore on hand for live data and match insights, this campaign arrives with purpose.
[...]
Across their last ten friendlies, Canada posted four wins, five draws and only one defeat. The run started with a 3-0 victory over Romania and a 1-0 win against Wales. A tight 0-1 loss to Australia followed, then goalless draws with Colombia and Ecuador. Momentum returned with a 2-0 win away to Venezuela and a 1-0 home win against Guatemala. In 2026 they drew 2-2 with Iceland, then 0-0 with Tunisia, before closing with a 2-0 win over Uzbekistan. Eight clean sheets in those ten games show a defense in good working order. For a team eyeing history at a World Cup, that kind of stability is gold.
[...]
Head coach J. Marsch arrives with a 15-7-8 record, a base that suggests clear ideas and consistency. Several standouts shape the spine of this team. A. Davies has a 6.82 Sofascore Rating in the 25/26 Bundesliga season. J. David carries a 6.42 in Serie A, while I. Koné shows 6.99 in Serie A as well. T. Buchanan adds width with a 6.79 in LaLiga, and P. David owns a 6.68 in the Pro League. On Sofascore, 10 is a perfect Rating, so these numbers sketch a balanced core rather than a one-man show. With Canada’s first World Cup goal arriving in 2022, the next step is clear. If this core turns club form into sharp international minutes, Group B could open up quickly.
[...]
A disciplined defense, like we saw in those eight clean sheets, sets the platform. One goal can swing tight group games, especially against compact opponents. Switzerland will likely test Canada’s nerves in key moments, while Bosnia and Herzegovina bring aerial and set-piece battles. Qatar should demand patience and control of tempo. For the hosts, banking early points is the shortest path to history. A first win is the immediate target and a knockout ticket is not a stretch from there. Keep an eye on live Sofascore match pages for in-game momentum and every Sofascore Rating swing. If the recent trend holds, Canada will give their fans plenty to track.
